text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS

- State attorney Juan Cesareo Ortiz Urculo called Supreme Court in the middle of its deliberations about whether to call former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez to testify about a 1980s "dirty war" against Basque separatists.
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar sees dialogue with ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) if the separatist rebels ever lay down their arms.
- Spanish clergy in Zaire says now is not the time to flee the country because its people are suffering.
EL MUNDO
- Public prosecutor Rogelio Gomez Guillamon will ask Supreme Court to decide in favour of government declassifying military intelligence papers about dirty war.
DIARIO 16
- General Council of the Judiciary supports press against government by rejecting draft law on official secrets.
- Veterans of International Brigades "conquer" streets of Madrid during 60th anniversary hommage to their fight during Spain's 1936-39 Civil War.
ABC
- Aznar in Bilbao: "There is no room for dialogue with ETA."
CINCO DIAS
- Entrecanales to be quoted on stock exchange after merger with Cubiertas.
- Ruling Popular Party (PP) denies 200,000 home-owners who are forced to keep rents low the fiscal benefits they were promised under previous Socialist government.
- Bourse and bonds hit maximums, caught up in Euro-optimism.
- Judge justifies women earning less.
EXPANSION
- Euphoric climate in markets propelled upwards by Wall Street.
- Brussels sees Spain in European economic and monetary union for first time.
- Cubiertas increases capital and absorbs Entrecanales.
- Employment Minister Javier Arenas says healthcare needs equivalent of Toledo pact on pensions to control medicine costs and erase fraud.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Aznar pledges to develop Basque autonomy.
- Spaniards saved 141,000 pesetas per head in 1995.
